# 5 Useful Sleeping Tips

## 1. Stick to a Consistent Sleep Schedule
- Going to bed and waking up at the same time every day regulates your body's internal clock (circadian rhythm)
- A consistent schedule makes it easier to fall asleep and wake up naturally
- Even on weekends, maintaining your schedule prevents "social jet lag" which can disrupt your sleep pattern

## 2. Create a Relaxing Bedtime Routine
- Winding down signals to your brain that it is time to sleep
- Activities like reading or light stretching reduce cortisol (stress hormone) levels
- A routine helps transition your mind from alertness to a restful state more efficiently

## 3. Avoid Screens Before Bed
- Phones and computers emit blue light which suppresses the production of melatonin, the sleep hormone
- Stimulating content from social media or television keeps your brain mentally active
- Reducing screen time at least one hour before bed allows melatonin levels to rise naturally

## 4. Keep Your Bedroom Cool and Dark
- The body naturally lowers its core temperature during sleep, so a cool room supports this process
- Darkness triggers the brain to produce more melatonin, encouraging deeper sleep
- Eliminating light and heat reduces the chances of waking up during the night

## 5. Limit Caffeine and Alcohol Intake
- Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors, which are responsible for making you feel sleepy
- Caffeine can remain in your system for **up to 6 hours**, so avoiding it in the afternoon is recommended
- Although alcohol may make you feel drowsy, it disrupts REM sleep and reduces overall sleep quality
